notes.title: Organizing features that nest, share a page, or share a component
notes.body:
Separate the kinds of relation instead of forcing one tree. (1) Part of: a card has at most one parent, two levels deep (parent → cards → steps); a step that grows gets promoted to a card. (2) Area: where it lives (a page, surface, or package), several cards per area, inferred by Claude from the files it touches, renameable. (3) Links: uses / blocks / related, many-to-many; a shared component is its own card that others use. Views: group by area or parent, parent rows roll up children's progress, a focus view per parent or area. Claude files new cards under the active parent and sets area from files; the user only corrects.

Who does what. Claude: create areas from files and name them; file each new card under the active parent and into an area; promote a step that grows into a child card; link cards that touch the same component; keep parent progress and 'can't be Done with open children'; flag drift ('this area has 14 cards, split it?'). Automatic, no Claude needed: rollups, grouping, 'used by N'. The user: rename or merge areas once; drag a card to another parent or area when Claude guessed wrong; decide what counts as a big parent (the product's shape); answer the occasional 'split this?' question. Never: create areas, tag cards, or file things by hand.
notes.considered: One strict tree (Jira epics) forces a choice between 'lives on Settings' and 'part of Billing'. Tags alone go stale and don't roll up. A free graph is expressive but unreadable in a list. Deep nesting turns into filing work.

notes.title: Board at a real URL: pros, cons and user fears
notes.body: Hosted page (useclipped.dev/app) talking to the local server. Pros: memorable/shareable link, UI updates on deploy, feels like a product, data stays local, room for sign-in later. Cons: dead when the local server is off; Chrome local-network prompt, Safari may block https→localhost; hosted page vs old local server version mismatch; deployment + domain + origin allowlist to maintain; bigger attack surface if the allowlist is wrong. Fears: 'is my plan on your server?' (biggest), the scary local-network prompt, 'why install if it's a website', 'can others open my board', lock-in if the site dies, analytics on the page, ad blockers/corporate networks. Mitigations: 'nothing is uploaded' banner, explain before the prompt, clear server-off screen with the start command, keep localhost:4747 as fallback, no analytics on the board page. Lean: clipped.localhost:4747 now; hosted page once sign-in/teams exist.
notes.considered: Tunnel (ngrok): real public URL but boards on the internet — rejected.

Message should be: you don't need to do anything, work with Claude and this fills itself. Ideas: (1) honest empty state panel, hide zero stats and + New card; (2) 'Start here' from their own Claude Code folders; (3) live 'listening for your first card' + first-card animation; (4) read-only sample project (Ledgerly) to explore, hideable; (5) 3-step checklist that ticks itself; (6) tour of board parts once ~3 cards exist; (7) a copyable first prompt. notes.title: First run: what we know, and a guided test session
notes.body: Known at first open, locally: every folder they've used Claude Code in (name, path, last used) and per-folder session counts/active time. Not known: what the projects are about (we never read conversations). Could add safely: project name/description from package.json or README, language, git state. They almost always open the board via /clipped:board inside a session, so board ui can pass the current folder: 'You're in 247News — want to see Clipped work there?'. Guided test: 'Try it in 2 minutes' copies one line — mkdir -p ~/clipped-try && cd ~/clipped-try && claude "<prompt that yields a feature with steps, an idea, a question, a review>" — and the page becomes a live checklist that ticks and explains each card type as it lands, ending 'That's Clipped'. Limits: Claude is steered not controlled (celebrate what happened, don't wait forever); the browser can't start Claude (one paste); scratch folder is the safe default.

notes.body:
Chose: two collections behind five tabs. A question is a card because it has a next step and an end. Brainstorms, plans and references are lighter notes with no status. The rule: a card has a next step, a note doesn't.
Why: user: ideas, market research and references come up mid-flow, and "any idea tossed out or reference mentioned requires scrolling back and breaking the flow". The user then asked "can it be added as tabs?".

One click opens; newest 5–6, rest behind More; last few also on the welcome page. Dedupe restarts; fade links that stay dead; hide query strings (tokens) in the display; never leaves the machine.
